key_insight: Allowing finite training error and thermal noise reveals that robust, wide solution regions persist in non-convex neural networks beyond the zero-temperature OGP barrier.
engineering_relevance: This suggests that adding controlled stochasticity or relaxed losses can make hard training regimes more searchable while still supporting useful generalization.
method: Extended the frozen 1RSB picture from zero temperature to finite temperature.
Derived a smoothness-based criterion for when finite-temperature loss relaxations eliminate freezing.
Generalized the overlap gap property to finite-energy configurations and analyzed teacher-student generalization.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a finite-energy message-passing algorithm used in numerical experiments showing that thermal noise improves generalization in regimes where zero-temperature recovery is computationally hard.
watch_item: The guarantees depend on the model's loss smoothness and finite-temperature assumptions, so the effect may not transfer directly to architectures with different geometry or optimization dynamics.
paper_title: On the robustness of noisy solutions in non-convex neural networks
